problem:
Consider the vector space ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$ of all $2\times 2$ matrices over $R.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}$ is a linearly independent set in ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$
- $[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ${[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}$
- ${[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of ${\text{M}}_{2}(R)$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying True Statements About Sets of Vectors in a Matrix Vector Space

examples.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066905/assets/8c5e7ba97572e7e0a0c548f8877a609e85096c646854bc4c3d2a693943b20496.png)
is true if and only if $x_1=x_2=0.$ So, the set is linearly independent.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066905/assets/4688890d66d47e92b0e38e603e1b885125dc143a4582b11db92acbf5cdc74ab1.png)

- Statement III is false. For example, the matrix $[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]$ can't be written as a linear combination of 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066905/assets/697c21a322d1136432b9ac23f959e766f972b829d790d88dc6be4163dce83669.png)
since all these linear combinations result in matrices with the entry $a_{11} = 0\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066905/assets/0ba338d733e2510ece4a75c2f16acfd1e79f7edbce46232dba8480ab7f37a666.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector space ${R}_{3}[t]$ of all polynomials in the variable $t$ over $R$ with degrees at most $3.$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${1,t,{t}^{2},{t}^{3}}$ is a linearly independent set in ${R}_{3}[t]$
- ${t}^{3}-3t+8$ can be expressed as a linear combination of ${1,t,{t}^{2},{t}^{3}}$
- ${1,t,{t}^{2},{t}^{3}}$ is a basis of ${R}_{3}[t]$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed, the equation 

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot 1+{x}_{2}\cdot t+{x}_{3}\cdot {t}^{2}+{x}_{4}\cdot {t}^{3}=0,
$$

 
is true if and only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}={x}_{4}=0.$ So, the set is linearly independent.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,

$$
{t}^{3}-3t+8=8\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot t+0\cdot {t}^{2}+1\cdot {t}^{3}.
$$

- Statement III is true. Indeed, the set is linearly independent and for any polynomial in ${R}_{3}[t],$ we get 

$$
a{t}^{3}+b{t}^{2}+ct+d=d\cdot 1+c\cdot t+b\cdot {t}^{2}+a\cdot {t}^{3}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
